bib.title: LLM In-Context Recall is Prompt Dependent

read.skipped: Appendix D heatmaps are images; no text

question: How well do LLMs recall a fact placed in their prompt, and how does that depend on prompt content, model size, architecture, training and fine-tuning?
hypothesis: Recall measured by a single needle-in-a-haystack test is not representative of a model's overall ability; it depends on the prompt.
contributions: Needle-in-a-haystack recall across nine LLMs with three different needles
Analysis of effects of training-data conflict, parameter count, architecture/training strategy and fine-tuning on recall

method.summary: Insert one factoid (needle) into Paul Graham essay filler (haystack) at varied lengths and depths, ask a near-trivial question, and score the answer 1-5 with GPT-4 Turbo as judge. Three needles (PistachioAI, San Francisco, Thornfield Hollow) are run on nine models.
method.task: in-context factoid recall (needle in a haystack)

datasets.name: Paul Graham Essays (haystack filler)
datasets.preprocessing: Haystack length and needle position adjusted to coincide with sentence breaks

other.note: base trained with 8k window and sliding window attention per text
base trained at 32k, rope-theta 1e6, no sliding window attention

inference.samples: one response per (haystack length, depth) cell; 35x35=1225 cells per test per model, 25x25=625 for GPT-4 Turbo; 31,275 responses graded in total
inference.prompting: System message constant, then haystack with needle, then question. Model-specific templates (Llama, Mistral, OpenAI) in Appendix A.

parameters.length_unit: tokens from each model's own tokenizer

metrics.name: Recall
metrics.definition: Sum of judge scores (1-5) over all length/depth cells divided by total possible score (5 per cell)

eval.protocol: GPT-4 Turbo judge scores each response 1-5 against reference (Table 4, Appendix C prompt, via LangChain evaluations). No repeated runs or seeds stated. Judge scoring anomalies noted in Section 5.

prompts.text: You are a helpful AI assistant that answers a question using only the provided information.
PistachioAI received a patent before its Series A. / What did PistachioAI receive before its Series A?
The best thing to do in San Francisco is eat a sandwich and sit in Dolores Park on a sunny day. / What is the best thing to do in San Francisco?
The best thing to do in Thornfield Hollow is eat a sandwich and sit in Harmony Glen Nature Preserve on a sunny day. / What is the best thing to do in Thornfield Hollow?

Please act as an impartial judge and evaluate the quality of the response provided by an AI assistant ... accuracy: Score 1 ... Score 5 ... rate the response on a scale of 1 to 5 by strictly following this format: "[[rating]]"

results.quote: requiring grading of 31,275 responses following the criteria in Table 4

limits: Single run per cell, no seeds, decoding settings and temperature not stated.
No ablation of Mistral v0.2 changes, so the cause of its gain is speculation (authors concede).
GPT-3.5 version difference inferred from an OpenAI blog, not verified.
Judge (GPT-4 Turbo) can misscore: haystack artifacts altering the prompt meaning gave a low score to a sensible answer (Section 5).
GPT-4 Turbo tested on a smaller grid (25x25) to control cost.
Needle questions are near-trivial single-fact retrieval; says nothing about multi-fact reasoning.
Scores are near ceiling for most models, so differences are small except Mistral v0.1 and GPT-4 Turbo San Francisco.
Models from early 2024; Gemini 1.5 context figure cited only as background.
